name: Deterministic math
what: A drop-in replacement for Math whose sin, cos, tan, atan, atan2, asin, acos, exp, log, pow and hypot are fdlibm ports built only from + - * / and sqrt, so a simulation gives the same bits in Chrome, Safari, Firefox and Node. Includes a self-check of 97 recorded results and a seeded random generator.
use_when: a simulation is re-run from its inputs somewhere else and must come out identical: replays or ghosts stored as inputs, share links, lockstep multiplayer, server-checked scores, bots or level solvers in Node, a daily puzzle from a seed

third_party.what: fdlibm math library (algorithms and coefficients; notice kept)
third_party.author: Sun Microsystems

third_party.what: musl libc's C versions of fdlibm, which the port follows
third_party.author: Rich Felker et al.

good_for: replays and ghosts, share links that re-simulate, lockstep multiplayer, verifying scores on a server, headless bots and level solvers whose results must hold in every browser, seeded daily challenges
not_for: rendering, shaders, cameras or anything only drawn (GPUs are not bit-exact and it does not matter there); games where only one machine ever simulates; huge angles past about 1e6 radians
how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs meticulai-deterministic-math, then put `import { DMath as Math } from '<path>/vendor/meticulai-deterministic-math/src/dmath.js';` at the top of each simulation file; see HOW-TO-USE.md
